Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: SONGS/ ORAL POETRY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learni
Topic 3.2: Poetry 3.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry 3.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry, part of SONGS/ ORAL POETRY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learni in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can one become a good poet? 2. How can you tell whether a poem is well written?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry 3.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology when searching online or offline for the steps

involved in the writing of a poem and present findings in class.

26

● Self- efficacy: This is promoted as the learner exhibits self-management when planning and composing a poem and shares

with peers.

Values:
● Responsibility: This is fostered as the learner looks out for constructive views when brainstorming for ideas, images and

phrases related to the topic identified.

● Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner assesses peer’s work objectively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Conservation: This is enhanced as the learner writes poems on environmental education and climate change.
